chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from one of our companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a group of people who sent their dogs, and all of them were trained, and they had named (Bismillah) over them. So when the dogs went, a strange dog joined them, whose owner they did not know, so they all participated in the hunt. He (peace be upon him) said: 'It should not be eaten from, because you do not know whether it was seized by a trained dog or not.'
ai.seo_question: Is the prey halal if an unknown dog joins the trained hunting dogs?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia legal principle of 'fear of doubt' (khawf al-shubha) in ritual purity, where the presence of an unverified participant invalidates the certainty of the act. It highlights the rigorous standards of Shia jurisprudence, requiring that the specific conditions of the command (such as the dog being trained and named) remain uncontaminated by unknown variables to ensure the prey's permissibility.
